content: The medication is indicated for reducing the incidence of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis (RVVC) in females who have a history of RVVC and are not of reproductive potential. It is contraindicated in females of reproductive potential, as well as in pregnant and lactating females. Females who are not of reproductive potential are defined as biological females who are postmenopausal or have other reasons for permanent infertility, such as tubal ligation, hysterectomy, or salpingo-oophorectomy. The safety and effectiveness of this medication have not been established in premenarchal females. Oteseconazole, a BCRP (Breast Cancer Resistance Protein) inhibitor, has the potential to increase the effects and toxicity risks of drugs that are BCRP substrates. This includes medications such as pitavastatin, alpelisib, atorvastatin, chlorothiazide, cimetidine, daunorubicin, dipyridamole, doxorubicin, ethinylestradiol, fluvastatin, glyburide, imatinib, irinotecan, lapatinib, ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, leflunomide, lenvatinib, methotrexate, mitoxantrone, nitrofurantoin, osimertinib, ozanimod, pantoprazole, pazopanib, riociguat, seladelpar, selexipag, selumetinib, sofosbuvir, sulfasalazine, talazoparib, tenofovir alafenamide (AF), tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (DF), topotecan, ubrogepant, velpatasvir, vemurafenib, voclosporin, and voxilaprevir. When co-administering oteseconazole with these drugs, it is recommended to use the lowest starting dose of the BCRP substrate or consider reducing the dose of the BCRP substrate. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored for potential adverse effects and toxicities. In particular, co-administration with nephrotoxic drugs may increase the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. For drugs like seladelpar, monitoring for adverse effects is specifically advised when used with BCRP inhibitors.
